They are alternatively referred to as tratados ("pacts" or "deals"). The firmas often incorporate lines, arrows, circles, and crosses, as well as skulls, suns, and moons. As they facilitate contact between the worlds, the firmas are deemed to be caminos ("roads"). The firmas are akin to the vèvè employed in Haitian Vodou and the anaforuanas used by Abakuá members. Firmas may derive from the sigils employed in European ceremonial magic traditions. However, some of the designs commonly found in firmas, such as that of the sun circling the Earth and of a horizon line dividing the worlds, are probably borrowed from traditional Kongo cosmology.
